text:
maria: heads up — during the 03:00 replay I saw steady RSS growth on pool-b GPUs. digging showed KV entries for small prefixes (2-6 tokens) persisting across many unrelated sessions.
kevin: what do you mean by persisting? evicted TTLs not firing?
maria: eviction TTLs are configured, but residency counts never drop. looks like same cache key is being minted for different requests, so eviction heuristics don't catch them as duplicates.
anjali: do you have an example key? might be a namespace or hashing mismatch.
maria: example (redacted): `prefix:v1:tenant=acme:prompt_sha=ab12cd:session_hint=none`. we see `session_hint` flipping between `none` and `sticky` but the rest matches, so entries don't coalesce.
sam: is the fingerprinting using full prompt bytes or normalized tokens? we changed sanitization recently right?
maria: token-normalized hash. but we also append `session_id` for longctx sessions in the client-side keypath when context > 1024 tokens. that seems to create unique keys even for identical prefixes.
kevin: ah ok — that would defeat cross-request reuse. is this new client behavior rolled?
maria: rolled to canary two weeks ago. low traffic, but under replay it amplifies.
anjali: two follow-ups: 1) can we make `session_id` optional for prefix-level keys and only attach it to per-session caches? 2) add a residency counter and last-access timestamp to decide eviction by LRU instead of strict TTL.
sam: +1 for residency counter. TTL-only is brittle for bursty workloads. we also should avoid mixing session-scoped and global prefix keys in the same namespace.
maria: agreed. quick mitigation: treat keys with `session_id` as session-scoped and map them to a small ephemeral slab that gets aggressively reclaimed. That reduces fragmentation impact while we fix hashing.
kevin: implementation note — prefer avoiding a global namespace flag. maybe encode scope in key prefix: `s:` for session, `g:` for global. cheap to change and reversible.
anjali: also want perf telemetry: emit `cache_coalesced:bool` per hit so we can see true reuse rates post-fix.
sam: for rollout plan: patch client to stop appending session_id for prefixes, ship server change to recognize `s:`/`g:` prefixes, and add residency counter. then canary 10% traffic.
maria: I'm going to open a quick bug + ops runbook. will include the heap profiles and a small script to replay the offending workload.
sre-bot: incident-created #INC-2026: kv-prefix-fragmentation — paging eviction spike observed. pager on-call notified.
kevin: thanks — I'll take the patch for the server side. assigning to kevin.
january: (note: realistic slack has typos)
anjali: haha january? ignore.
maria: pinging infra for rotation of the canary tonight at 00:30 to validate the slab reclamation approach.
kevin: I'll prototype the key-scope change and residency counter today. sending a short RFC in eng-runtime.
maria: thanks all. i'll paste heap diff and the minimal replay commands in the ticket. :thumbsup:
